question:
What is the mode of the following data?

5, 7, 6, 5, 9, 8, 6, 7, 11, 10, 5, 7, 6, 8, 6, 9, 10, 6
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mode of any given data set is simply the value that occurs most frequently.

By a quick visual scan of the numbers: 5, 7, 6, 5, 9, 8, 6, 7, 11, 10, 5, 7, 6, 8, 6, 9, 10, 6

We can clearly see that the number '6' appears more times than any other number.

Since '6' occurs 5 times, which is the maximum, it is the mode.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The data set: 5, 7, 6, 5, 9, 8, 6, 7, 11, 10, 5, 7, 6, 8, 6, 9, 10, 6

**Formula Used:**

Mode = The observation with the highest frequency in a data set.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us list the frequencies by counting each distinct value:

⇒ Frequency of 5 = 3

⇒ Frequency of 6 = 5

⇒ Frequency of 7 = 3

⇒ Frequency of 8 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 9 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 10 = 2

⇒ Frequency of 11 = 1

⇒ Since the maximum frequency is 5, the mode corresponds to the data value 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean

The mean is the basic average of all numbers, calculated as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations.

Median

The median is the exactly middle value when a data set is ordered from least to greatest. If there is an even number of observations, it is the average of the two middlemost values.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, Mean, Median, and Mode are mathematically related by the formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Bimodal Data

If two distinct data values share the exact same highest frequency, the data set is said to have two modes and is classified as bimodal.
